questions.q: Why is IPv4's address space considered too small for today's internet?
options: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits, capping the space at about 4.3 billion addresses — nowhere near enough for billions of connected devices
IPv4 was never designed to support more than 1,000 devices
IPv4 addresses expire and must be renewed, unlike IPv6
IPv4 only works on wired connections, never wireless
questions.explain: IPv4's 32-bit address space tops out around 4.3 billion unique addresses, which is far too small for a planet full of phones, laptops, servers, and IoT devices.

questions.q: How large is IPv6's address space compared to IPv4's?
options: Exactly double IPv4's address space
About the same size, just written differently
128 bits, roughly 340 undecillion addresses — large enough that exhaustion isn't a realistic concern
IPv6 has fewer total addresses than IPv4, but they're distributed more efficiently
questions.explain: IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, giving a practically inexhaustible address space compared to IPv4's 32 bits.

questions.q: What does collapsing 2001:0db8:85a3:0000:0000:8a2e:0370:7334 using both IPv6 shorthand rules produce?
options: 2001:db8:85a3:0:0:8a2e:0370:7334 (no further shortening possible)
questions.explain: Dropping leading zeros in each group and collapsing the one run of consecutive all-zero groups to :: produces 2001:db8:85a3::8a2e:370:7334.

questions.q: Why can the :: shorthand only appear once in a single IPv6 address?
options: It's a stylistic preference with no technical reason
Using it twice would make it ambiguous how many zero groups each :: represents
IPv6 addresses are only allowed to have one zero group total
:: can actually be used as many times as needed in one address
questions.explain: If :: appeared twice, there would be no way to know how many zero groups belong to each collapsed section, so the standard allows only one :: per address.

options: Running two separate physical network cables for redundancy
A device or network running IPv4 and IPv6 simultaneously, using whichever the destination supports
A firewall configuration that blocks all IPv6 traffic
Running IPv6 only, with IPv4 fully disabled
questions.explain: Dual-stack is the realistic migration path most organizations use today — IPv4 and IPv6 running side by side on the same device or network.
